analyst_view.overall: Sixth-placed Burgos (24 points) host 19th-placed Albacete (13 points) on Sunday night at El Plantío. Burgos, under Sergio Francisco, saw a four-game unbeaten run end with a 3-1 loss at Leganés; they are a set-piece threat who fill the box, but are without forwards Jon Karrikaburu and David González and also Brais Martínez, of whom only González is in the numbers. Albacete have been transformed under Joseba Etxeberria, with four straight league wins (latest 1-0 v Celta Fortuna), a high press and quick counters, though they are still in the bottom four. Albacete miss Puertas, Obeng, Fran Gámez, Higinio Marín, Javi Moreno and the suspended José Corpas, most of them out for weeks; striker Munir is close to returning and Sanba has ankle inflammation. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take about 11% off Burgos's goals for David González. Karrikaburu is out too and the numbers don't know it, leaving Burgos short of forwards against an Albacete side that has kept things tight during its winning run, so I trim a little, to about 2.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 5.5 of them Burgos's, a side that attacks wide with quick full-backs and lives off set pieces. Albacete's press could push Burgos into more long balls, but that does not clearly change corners, so I stay at 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards. Albacete's pressing and Burgos's physical centre-backs could mean some duels, but nothing suggests extra needle and no referee is named, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, 17 of them Burgos's. With Karrikaburu and Brais Martínez out beyond what the numbers know, and Albacete's high press making Burgos play longer, I expect fewer home shots and trim to about 25.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Burgos's missing forwards should mean slightly fewer clear chances, so I trim a little, to about 7.8.
